root_cause.text: `ip6t_eui64` in `net/ipv6/netfilter/ip6t_eui64.c` only validated the skb MAC header when `par->fragoff != 0`, allowing `eui64_mt6()` to call `eth_hdr(skb)` on packets with an invalid or absent MAC header when `fragoff == 0`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `&& par->fragoff != 0` from the guard that checks `skb_mac_header(skb) >= skb->head && skb_mac_header(skb) + ETH_HLEN <= skb->data`, and the CVE description states that with `par->fragoff == 0` the function could still reach `eth_hdr(skb)` even when the MAC header was not valid.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix eui64_mt6() to unconditionally hotdrop packets with invalid MAC header bounds instead of depending on fragment offset.
intent_record.what: The condition in eui64_mt6() was changed by removing the trailing "&& par->fragoff != 0" from the if-statement that checks whether the skb MAC header is within bounds and fully precedes skb->data. As a result, the hotdrop-and-fail path now triggers solely based on the MAC header bounds check.
intent_record.how: Runtime behavior now rejects packets whenever the MAC header is invalid or inaccessible, regardless of fragment offset. Previously, the rejection only occurred when that bounds check failed and par->fragoff was nonzero, which could allow some invalid cases to bypass hotdrop in non-fragmented traffic.

grouping_result.intent: Fix eui64_mt6() to unconditionally hotdrop packets with invalid MAC header bounds instead of depending on fragment offset.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes ip6t_eui64/eui64_mt6() so invalid or absent MAC headers are always rejected, rather than only being checked when fragoff is nonzero.

candidates.rationale: This check was part of the pre-fix condition that only rejected invalid MAC headers when combined with `par->fragoff != 0`, leaving packets with invalid or absent MAC headers unchecked when `fragoff == 0`.

This is the bounds check on the MAC header, but in the vulnerable code it was not enforced unconditionally; its effect was gated by fragment offset, enabling `eth_hdr(skb)` to be used on invalid headers.

vuln_statements.explanation: This fragment-offset condition gated the MAC-header validity check, so packets with fragoff == 0 bypassed the safeguard and could reach eth_hdr(skb) with an invalid or absent MAC header.
This is the first half of the MAC-header bounds check that was only applied when the fragoff gate allowed it, contributing to the unsafe access path.
This bounds check was part of the validation that should have protected eth_hdr(skb), but it was incorrectly conditioned on fragoff != 0 in the vulnerable code.
